html:
SMTO-SKL-0182 — GitHub refused this change in its current state

GUID: 1f5dc3e8-bf42-50d4-9672-007bd71f5617
Slug: github-precondition-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub refused the change because the item on GitHub isn't in the state the request expected. For example, it was edited since SMTO last looked, a name or value isn't accepted, or the release is already published. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the item on github.com (the issue, pull request, file or release) and see whether someone changed it recently or whether your change is already there. GitHub turns down a change made against an older version of the item.
  2. Check that any names you gave exist on GitHub, such as labels, people to assign, branches or tags. GitHub rejects values it doesn't recognize for this project.
  3. Ask the Agent to look at the item again and then make the change, giving any corrected names. Nothing was changed this time, so one request based on the current state is safe.

What success looks like

  • The change appears on the item on github.com and the Agent reports it as applied.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the GitHub project, with a link to the item you were changing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GitHub returned 409, 412 or 422 for an operation without a more specific error class (for example a stale file sha, an invalid label or assignee, or a duplicate release), or release_publish found the target release is no longer a draft.

What this means

  • GitHub returns HTTP 409/412/422 outside specific operation classes, or release publication preflight finds the target is not a draft. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • GitHub returns HTTP 409/412/422 outside specific operation classes, or release publication preflight finds the target is not a draft.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual validation/conflict response or release draft state instead of assuming every failure is a changed revision.

How to fix it

  • Read the exact object again (github.issue, github.pull_request, github.release, github.contents, etc.) and compare it with the request: refresh any file sha, check labels/assignees/tag names exist, and for release_publish confirm the release is still draft=true. Correct the arguments and obtain a fresh confirmation before sending one new write.
  • Inspect the exact provider object and validation requirements. Correct the request and obtain confirmation for any changed mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate operation satisfies its exact current preconditions.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
